title: Mimicking and Measuring Occlusal Erosive Tooth Wear with the "Rub&Roll" and Non-contact Profilometry
protocol: Collect 24 sound extracted human (pre)molars from dental practices.
Brush each tooth with pumice using a low-speed handpiece to achieve a clean and smooth surface.
Rinse each tooth for 15 seconds under running tap water.
Embed the samples to fit them into the recesses of the cylinder device measuring 12 mm x 15 mm x 27.5 mm.
Melt one stick (113 g) of impression compound on a hotplate at 50 °C for approximately 10 minutes.
Dip the occlusal part of each molar into the molten substance to cover the occlusal surface completely.
Place each molar upside down on a microscope slide, pressing until all cup tips touch the glass and wait about 30 seconds until the impression compound has cooled and set.
Mix 13 g polymer with 10 mL monomer for PMMA in a fume hood for roughly 25 seconds using a spatula.
Leave the mixed PMMA to stand for 15 seconds to allow air bubbles to escape.
Turn each microscope slide upside down and suspend the molar in the silicone mold filled with PMMA mixture.
Press the slide down until it touches the mold, ensuring proper alignment of the tooth within the mold.
Set PMMA at room temperature and 1,000 hPa for 20 min.
Remove the microscope slide and embedded tooth from the silicon mold.
Measure the total height of the embedded molar.
Adjust the height to exactly 27.3 mm by incrementally removing cured PMMA with a milling machine equipped with a milling cutter of 16 mm.
Add 0.1 M lactic acid (50 g) to a stirring plate.
Add 1.5 mM CaCl2 (1.103 g) to the solution on the stirring plate.
Add 0.9 mM KH2PO4 (0.612 g) to the solution on the stirring plate.
Add 10 mL of 1% chloramine to the solution on the stirring plate.
Add 0.5 ppm F (2.5 mL of 1,000 ppm Fluorid Standard solution) to the solution on the stirring plate.
Add 4,900 mL of deionized water to the solution on the stirring plate.
Titrate with 10 M KOH (± 50 mL) to pH 4.8 using a calibrated pH glass electrode.
Remove the cylinder from the container and place 24 specimens in the recesses in the cylinder of the Rub&Roll.
Adjust loading force by placing a shim under the specimen: use no shim for no load, a 1 mm shim for 30 N, and a 1.5 mm shim for 50 N.
Mount the two parts of the cylinder and secure it with an M6 bolt.
Place the secured cylinder in the container filled with demineralization solution.
Place the loading rod consisting of a PVC tube with an outer diameter of 14 mm, inner diameter of 10 mm, and a stainless steel insert of 9 mm diameter.
Set the rotation speed to 20 rpm.
Replace the demineralization solution and PVC tube twice a week.
Check the pH of the demineralization solution twice a week using a calibrated glass electrode.
Disconnect the cylinder from the container after 3 months.
Remove the specimen by disassembling two parts of the cylinder.
Store the specimen in deionized water.
Scan the sample before and after loading using a non-contact profilometer.
Switch on the computer, PSU module, and sensor controller for profilometric scanning.
Place the appropriate sensor and secure it with a thumbscrew.
Insert the optical fiber into the sensor controller carefully.
Select the correct sensor from the options displayed on the sensor controller menu.
Press F3 and scroll to 2 - 10,000 µm.
Select (10 mm) and press F4.
Press F1 and choose F4 to save settings to EEPROM.
Select LED intensity and turn to position "± 9 o'clock".
Press F4 - F2 - F4 to take a "dark reference" of the sensor.
Open the software and choose the option "connect" to the device.
Choose Tools in the menu bar followed by sensor selection and choose Sensor S29 | 10 - 10,000 µm.
Choose Tools in the menu bar followed by sample rate and choose 300 Hz.
Choose Tools in the menu bar followed by speed sensor and choose 0 - 100%.
Select Scan in the menu bar.
Select Key Move Stage.
Press the yellow area in the middle of the screen to move the measuring table to the center.
Position the specimen in the center of the measuring table, followed by setting the correct height within the range of the sensor.
Place the sensor above the area of interest of the specimen and adjust the distance of the sensor so that the complete sample area to be scanned is located within the focus range of the sensor.
Choose Settings.
Set the average to 2.
Press OK to return to main scanning setup.
Position the sensor beam on the upper left corner of the specimen.
Set the total scan area to 15 mm x 12 mm.
Set the step size in X and Y direction to 40 µm (0.04 mm).
Press Scan now to start scanning.
Select File in the menu bar, followed by choosing Save As when the scan is finished.
Select File in the menu bar, followed by choosing Open file.
Select Warpage in the menu bar.
Apply a warpage filter of 1.
Select Highest point in the menu bar.
Find the highest point on the molar.
Select Tools in the menu bar, followed by choosing option-scale to the scan configuration.
Set the offset in mm calculated by Z value highest point (measured) - 3500.
Set the Range in manual from 0 to 3.6 mm.
Press OK.
Select Load Area in the menu bar to reset the scale.
Select File in the menu bar, followed by choosing Save As.
Subtract scans taken at two different moments in time.
Select Open in the software menu bar.
Locate and select the original scan file.
Locate and select the modified scan file.
Press OK to open the selected files.
Choose manual leveling option on the Options screen.
Apply compensation offset to the original scan.
Apply compensation offset to the modified scan.
Select Window in the menu bar.
Create a new view.
Choose cross section view from the options.
Select the modified surface.
Move the modified surface horizontally over the original surface using control and left/right arrow keys.
Move the modified surface vertically over the original surface using control and up/down arrow keys.
Adjust the height (Z direction) of the modified surface using shift and up/down arrow keys to minimize subtracted volume and height.
Select File in the menu bar.
Choose Save As from the options.
